description: Design a 32-bit adder in Verilog that takes two 32-bit inputs and produces a 32-bit sum and a carry-out signal. The module should be able to handle overflow correctly.

Design a simple memory allocation system where a memory block can be allocated and freed. The system should have an input to request memory allocation and another input to free the memory. The output should reflect the current memory status: allocated or free.
code:
module memory_allocator (  
    input clk,  
    input reset,  
    input [1:0] request, // 00: free, 01: allocate, 10: status check  
    output reg allocated // 0: free, 1: allocated  
);  
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            allocated <= 0;  
        end else begin  
            case (request)  
                2'b00: allocated <= 0; // free memory  
                2'b01: allocated <= 1; // allocate memory  
                2'b10: allocated <= allocated; // check status, no change  
                default: allocated <= allocated;  
            endcase  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design a Support Vector Machine (SVM) inspired circuit that classifies 2D points based on their coordinates (x, y). The circuit should output a binary classification: `1` for points above the decision boundary and `0` for points below the decision boundary. The decision boundary can be represented by the equation `y = mx + b`, where `m` is the slope and `b` is the y-intercept. Use fixed point representation for coordinates and parameters.

Create a Verilog module that implements a Monte Carlo simulation for a simple circuit. The module should take two inputs: a 5-bit random number and a control signal. Based on the control signal, the module will either output the squared value of the number if the control signal is high (1) or the inverted value of the number if the control signal is low (0). For the purpose of the simulation, consider the random number to be uniformly distributed in the range of 0 to 31.
code:
module monte_carlo_sim (
    input [4:0] random_num,
    input ctrl,
    output reg [4:0] output_num
);

always @(*) begin
    if (ctrl) begin
        output_num = random_num * random_num; // Squared value of random_num
    end else begin
        output_num = ~random_num; // Inverted value of random_num
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design a sample rate converter that takes an input signal of 8 bits and converts it to an output signal of 16 bits. Design a 2-bit barrel shifter that can shift input data left or right based on a control signal. The inputs to the shifter are a 2-bit data input (DATA) and a 1-bit control input (DIR). When DIR is 0, the shifter performs a left shift; when DIR is 1, it performs a right shift. The output should be a 2-bit result.
code:
module barrel_shifter(  
    input [1:0] DATA,  
    input DIR,  
    output reg [1:0] RESULT  
);  
    always @(*) begin  
        case (DIR)  
            1'b0: RESULT = DATA << 1; // Left shift  
            1'b1: RESULT = DATA >> 1; // Right shift  
            default: RESULT = 2'b00;  
        endcase  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that simulates a simple singly linked list traversal. The module should be able to initialize a linked list and traverse through its nodes to output their values one by one. The linked list will be defined with a fixed size of 5 nodes, and the values will be provided as input during initialization. The module should also indicate when the end of the list is reached.

Design a current sensor system in Verilog that measures the current flowing through a load. The system should have the following specifications:
- The input to the system will be a 4-bit value representing the current in milliamps (mA).
- The output of the system will be a 3-bit value, which indicates whether the current is low (000), normal (001), or high (010) based on the input.
- The thresholds for current ranges are as follows:
  - Low: 0 - 4 mA
  - Normal: 5 - 9 mA
  - High: 10 mA and above
- The system should have a clock input for synchronization and a reset input to clear the output.
code:
module current_sensor (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [3:0] current_input,
    output reg [2:0] current_status
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            current_status <= 3'b000; // Reset output
        end else begin
            case (current_input)
                4'b0000: current_status <= 3'b000; // 0 mA
                4'b0001: current_status <= 3'b000; // 1 mA
                4'b0010: current_status <= 3'b000; // 2 mA
                4'b0011: current_status <= 3'b000; // 3 mA
                4'b0100: current_status <= 3'b000; // 4 mA
                4'b0101: current_status <= 3'b001; // 5 mA
                4'b0110: current_status <= 3'b001; // 6 mA
                4'b0111: current_status <= 3'b001; // 7 mA
                4'b1000: current_status <= 3'b001; // 8 mA
                4'b1001: current_status <= 3'b001; // 9 mA
                default: current_status <= 3'b010; // 10 mA and above
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Implement a FIFO (First In, First Out) queue in Verilog. The FIFO should support the following operations: enqueue (add an item to the end of the queue), dequeue (remove an item from the front of the queue), and check if the queue is empty. Design a finite state machine (FSM) that keeps track of the state of a robot in a 2D grid for SLAM. The robot can move in four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and must update its current position accordingly. The input to the FSM will be the direction of movement, and the output will be the new position of the robot on the grid. The initial position of the robot is (0,0).
code:
module robot_slam_fsm(  
    input clk,  
    input reset,  
    input [1:0] direction, // 00: UP, 01: DOWN, 10: LEFT, 11: RIGHT  
    output reg [7:0] x_pos,  
    output reg [7:0] y_pos  
);  
    initial begin  
        x_pos = 8'b00000000;  
        y_pos = 8'b00000000;  
    end  
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            x_pos <= 8'b00000000;  
            y_pos <= 8'b00000000;  
        end else begin  
            case (direction)  
                2'b00: y_pos <= y_pos + 1; // UP  
                2'b01: y_pos <= y_pos - 1; // DOWN  
                2'b10: x_pos <= x_pos - 1; // LEFT  
                2'b11: x_pos <= x_pos + 1; // RIGHT  
                default: begin  
                    x_pos <= x_pos;  
                    y_pos <= y_pos;  
                end  
            endcase  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design a 128-bit AES encryption module that takes a 128-bit plaintext and a 128-bit key as inputs and produces a 128-bit ciphertext as output. The module should implement the AES encryption algorithm using a simplified version suitable for simulation and testing purposes.

Design a 3rd-order Chebyshev low-pass filter using Verilog. The filter should take a 4-bit signed input (representing the sampled signal) and produce a 4-bit signed output. The output should be calculated based on the previous three output values to implement the filter's transfer function.

Create a simple I2C controller that generates the I2C clock signal (SCL) and sends a start signal (START) when an input enable signal (EN) is high. The controller should also have an input data line (SDA) that it drives low when sending data bits.
code:
module I2C_Controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire EN,
    output reg SCL,
    output reg START,
    output reg SDA
);
    reg [3:0] count;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (EN) begin
            START <= 1'b1;  // Start condition
            count <= count + 1;
            SCL <= ~SCL;     // Toggle clock
            if (count == 4'd8) begin
                SDA <= 1'b0; // Sending data (logic low)
                count <= 4'd0; // Reset count
            end
        end else begin
            START <= 1'b0; // Stop condition when EN is low
            SCL <= 1'b0;   // Ensure SCL is low
            SDA <= 1'b1;   // Release SDA line
            count <= 4'd0; // Reset count
        end
    end
endmodule

description: A GPIO controller that manages the state of a GPIO pin based on input signals. The controller has an enable signal to allow or block input, a set signal to set the pin high, and a reset signal to set the pin low. The output pin should reflect these conditions with priority given to the set and reset signals when enabled.

Design a simple PCIe endpoint controller state machine that handles three states: IDLE, REQUEST, and ACKNOWLEDGE. The state machine should transition from IDLE to REQUEST on a 'start' signal, and from REQUEST to ACKNOWLEDGE on a 'request_done' signal. It should return to IDLE after a fixed duration in the ACKNOWLEDGE state, indicated by a 'timeout' signal.
code:
module pcie_endpoint_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input start,
    input request_done,
    input timeout,
    output reg [1:0] state // 2-bit state representation
);

    // State encoding
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00;
    parameter REQUEST = 2'b01;
    parameter ACKNOWLEDGE = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= REQUEST;
                    end
                end
                
                REQUEST: begin
                    if (request_done) begin
                        state <= ACKNOWLEDGE;
                    end
                end
                
                ACKNOWLEDGE: begin
                    if (timeout) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                end
                
                default: state <= IDLE; // Default case
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a 24-bit ADC (Analog to Digital Converter) controller in Verilog that takes an 8-bit input representing the analog value and outputs a 24-bit digital value. Design a simple 2-bit Branch Predictor that predicts the next branch direction based on the previous two outcomes. The predictor should have a 2-bit history register that updates on each clock cycle based on the current branch outcome (taken or not taken). The predictor should output the predicted branch direction (0 for not taken, 1 for taken).
code:
module branch_predictor (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input branch_outcome,  // 1 for taken, 0 for not taken
    output reg prediction   // 1 for taken, 0 for not taken
);
    reg [1:0] history; // 2-bit history register

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            history <= 2'b00; // reset history
            prediction <= 0;  // reset prediction
        end else begin
            prediction <= (history[1] == 1) ? 1 : 0; // prediction logic
            // Update history based on the current outcome
            history <= {history[0], branch_outcome};  
        end
    end
endmodule

Create a pulse generator that produces a single pulse of a specified width every time an input signal transitions from low to high. The pulse width is defined by a parameter, and the pulse should remain high for that duration before returning to low.

Design a 16-bit Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) controller in Verilog. The ADC controller should accept a 16-bit input data representing the analog value and provide a 1-bit output indicating whether the converted value is above a predefined threshold. The threshold is a 16-bit input to the ADC controller. If the ADC output is greater than or equal to the threshold, the output bit should be set to 1; otherwise, it should be 0. Design a 1-bit DRAM cell that can store a bit of data. The cell should have the following inputs and outputs:
1. `data_in`: The data to be written to the cell (1 bit)
2. `write_enable`: A control signal to enable writing to the cell (1 bit)
3. `data_out`: The data output from the cell (1 bit)
4. `reset`: A signal to reset the cell to 0 (1 bit)

The operation should be as follows: 
- When `write_enable` is high, the `data_in` value should be stored in the cell.
- When `reset` is high, the cell should be reset to 0 regardless of the `write_enable`.
- Otherwise, the cell should retain its previous value.
code:
module dram_cell (
    input wire data_in,
    input wire write_enable,
    input wire reset,
    output reg data_out
);

always @(posedge write_enable or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        data_out <= 1'b0; // Reset the cell to 0
    end else begin
        data_out <= data_in; // Store the input data
    end
end

endmodule

description:
Design a simple EEPROM cell that can read, write, and reset data. The EEPROM cell should have inputs for data (D), a write enable signal (WE), a read enable signal (RE), and an output for the stored data (Q). The behavior should be as follows: 
1. When WE is high, the input data D should be written to the output Q.
2. When RE is high, the output Q should reflect the stored data.
3. If both WE and RE are low, Q should hold its previous state.
code:
module eeprom_cell (
    input wire [7:0] D,     // Data input
    input wire WE,          // Write enable
    input wire RE,          // Read enable
    output reg [7:0] Q      // Data output
);

    always @(*) begin
        if (WE) begin
            Q = D;           // Write data to Q
        end else if (RE) begin
            // Read operation, Q retains its value

        end
        // If both WE and RE are low, Q holds its previous value
    end
endmodule

Design an 8-bit shift register with parallel load capability. The shift register should shift the data to the right on each clock cycle and load a new 8-bit value when the load signal is high. Design a simple Ethernet MAC controller that takes a data input and a control signal to either store the incoming data or transmit it. description: Design a simple Verilog module that implements a linked list traversal. The module will have inputs representing the head of the linked list and a control signal to perform the traversal. The output will be the value of the current node being pointed to in the linked list. The linked list is represented by an array of values, and the traversal will be done based on a clock signal.
code:
module linked_list_traversal (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [4:0] head,
    input start_traversal,
    output reg [4:0] current_value
);
    reg [4:0] nodes[0:4]; // Array of linked list nodes (5 nodes for simplicity)
    reg [2:0] index;

    // Initialize the linked list nodes
    initial begin
        nodes[0] = 5'd1; // Node 0
        nodes[1] = 5'd2; // Node 1
        nodes[2] = 5'd3; // Node 2
        nodes[3] = 5'd4; // Node 3
        nodes[4] = 5'd5; // Node 4
    end

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            index <= 3'd0; // Reset the index
            current_value <= 5'd0; // Reset the current value
        end else if (start_traversal) begin
            if (index < 3'd5) begin
                current_value <= nodes[index]; // Output current node value
                index <= index + 3'd1; // Move to the next node
            end
        end
    end

Design a UART controller that transmits a byte of data serially with a configurable baud rate. The UART controller should have the following inputs: a clock signal, a reset signal, a start signal (to begin transmission), an 8-bit data input, and a baud rate divisor. The output should be the transmitted serial data bit and a transmission complete signal. The transmission should occur bit by bit, starting from the least significant bit after the start signal is asserted.
code:
module uart_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    input wire [15:0] baud_div,
    output reg tx,
    output reg tx_complete
);
    reg [3:0] bit_cnt; // Counter for bits to be transmitted
    reg [15:0] baud_cnt; // Counter for baud rate
    reg [7:0] shift_reg; // Shift register for data transmission
    reg transmitting;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            tx <= 1'b1; // Idle state
            tx_complete <= 1'b0;
            bit_cnt <= 4'b0;
            baud_cnt <= 16'b0;
            transmitting <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (transmitting) begin
                baud_cnt <= baud_cnt + 1;
                if (baud_cnt >= baud_div) begin
                    baud_cnt <= 16'b0;
                    if (bit_cnt < 8) begin
                        tx <= shift_reg[bit_cnt]; // Transmit current bit
                        bit_cnt <= bit_cnt + 1; // Move to next bit
                    end else begin
                        tx <= 1'b1; // Stop bit
                        transmitting <= 1'b0;
                        tx_complete <= 1'b1; // Transmission complete
                    end
                end
            end else if (start) begin
                shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data into shift register
                bit_cnt <= 4'b0; // Reset bit count
                baud_cnt <= 16'b0; // Reset baud count
                tx <= 1'b0; // Start bit
                transmitting <= 1'b1; // Begin transmission
                tx_complete <= 1'b0; // Not complete yet
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire [3:0] req,
    output reg [3:0] grant
);

    if (reset) begin
        grant <= 4'b0000;
    end else begin
        grant <= 4'b0000; // Default to no grant
        casez (req)
            4'b1???: grant <= 4'b1000; // grant req[0]
            4'b01??: grant <= 4'b0100; // grant req[1]

module i2c_controller (
    input wire clk,          // Clock signal
    input wire start,        // Start signal
    input wire [7:0] data,   // Data to send
    output reg busy,         // Busy signal
    output reg scl,          // I2C clock line
    output reg sda           // I2C data line
);

    reg [3:0] state;        // State variable
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;    // Shift register for data

    // State machine
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case (state)
            0: begin
                busy <= 0;
                if (start) begin
                    shift_reg <= data;
                    state <= 1;
                end
            end
            1: begin
                busy <= 1;
                scl <= 0;         // Clock low
                sda <= shift_reg[7]; // Send MSB
                shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], 1'b0}; // Shift data
                state <= 2;
            end
            2: begin
                scl <= 1;         // Clock high
                state <= 3;
            end
            3: begin
                scl <= 0;         // Clock low again
                if (shift_reg != 8'b0) begin
                    state <= 1;   // Continue sending
                end else begin
                    busy <= 0;    // Transmission complete
                    state <= 0;   // Go back to idle
                end
            end
        endcase
    end
endmodule

    input [N*N-1:0] graph, // Adjacency matrix
    output reg [2*N-1:0] mst_edges // Output edges in the MST
);
    integer i, j, min_cost, u, v, total_edges;
    reg [N-1:0] selected;
    
    always @(*) begin
        mst_edges = 0;
        selected = 0;
        total_edges = 0;
        selected[0] = 1; // Start from the first vertex

        for (i = 0; i < N-1; i = i + 1) begin
            min_cost = 999999; // Set to a large number
            for (u = 0; u < N; u = u + 1) begin
                if (selected[u]) begin
                    for (v = 0; v < N; v = v + 1) begin
                        if (!selected[v] && graph[u*N + v] > 0 && graph[u*N + v] < min_cost) begin
                            min_cost = graph[u*N + v];
                            mst_edges[total_edges*4 +: 4] = {u, v}; // Store the edge
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
            selected[v] = 1; // Mark the selected vertex
            total_edges = total_edges + 1; // Increment edge count
        end
    end
endmodule

module pitch_detection (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input serial_data,
    output reg pitch_detected
);

    reg [3:0] state;    // State machine for pattern matching

    // Define the pitch detection pattern (simplified)
    parameter PATTERN = 4'b1010; // Example pattern for pitch detection

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 0;
            state <= 0;
            pitch_detected <= 0;
        end else begin
            // Increment the counter
            counter <= counter + 1;

            // Check for pattern on the serial data
            if (serial_data == PATTERN[state]) begin
                if (state == 3) begin
                    pitch_detected <= 1; // Pattern matched
                    state <= 0;          // Reset state
                end else begin
                    state <= state + 1; // Move to next pattern state
                end
            end else begin
                state <= 0; // Reset state if pattern is broken
                pitch_detected <= 0; // Reset detected signal
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    input K,
    input clk,
    output reg Q
);
